CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SHAILENDRA SINGH  ORAL ORDER 6 09-05-2025 I.A. No. 01 of 2025 Heard Mr. Babu Nandan Prasad, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr.
Ramchandra Singh, learned APP for the State.
2.

The present Interlocutory Application has been placed for consideration of appellant Baliram Singh's bail prayer made under Section 430(1) of the BNSS and suspension of his sentence during the pendency of his appeal.

3. This appeal has been filed against the judgment of conviction dated 28.06.2023 and order of sentence dated 05.07.2023 passed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI-cum- Special Judge, POCSO Act, Rohtas, Sasaram in connection with POCSO Case No. 72/ 2022, arising out of Kargahar P.S. Case No. 174 of 2022 whereby and whereunder Patna High Court CR.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
APP (SJ)
No.3264 of 2023(6) dt.09-05-2025 the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under section 376 read with section 511 of the IPC and under section 8 read with section 12 of POCSO Act and sentenced for the said offences.

4. The main submissions advanced by the appellant's counsel are that it is second attempt of the appellant to get the relief under section 430(1) of the BNSS and his first prayer was rejected vide order dated 18.04.2024 passed by this court but giving him a liberty to renew his prayer after one year from that order if his appeal is not taken up for hearing within the said period and now, the Baliram Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197997913/

sentences.text: appellant has renewed his prayer in the light of the said liberty and also on the ground of his present custody period which is about three years some days short.

It is further submitted that the appellant is an old person and the instant matter relates to the offence of attempt to rape and he has been awarded the punishment of 10 years of R.I. which is higher end of the punishment prescribed for the alleged offence and the appellant's appeal is of the year 2023 so there is a little chance of early hearing of his appeal.
5. Learned APP appearing for the State has chosen the written objection to oppose the appellant's present prayer which was filed when the appellant's first prayer was heard and Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.3264 of 2023(6) dt.09-05-2025 decided.

It is submitted by him that the instant matter relates to serious offence and the appellant attempted to outrage the modesty of a minor girl aged about 13 years and there are ample evidences to substantiate the allegation levelled against the appellant by the victim.
6. Heard both the sides and perused the relevant materials.

Though, there is serious allegation against the appellant but considering his present custody period, which has been about three years and also unlikelihood of his appeal to be taken up for hearing in near future as the same relates to the year 2023 and also taking into account the appellant's old age, this Court is now inclined to accept the bail prayer of the appellant made under Section 430(1) of the BNSS Accordingly, let the appellant above-named be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- ( Rs. Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge- VI-cum- Special Judge, POCSO Act, Rohtas,
Sasaram in connection with POCSO Case No. 72/ 2022, arising out of Kargahar P.S. Case No. 174 of 2022 7.
The execution of sentence of imprisonment shall remain suspended during the appellant's bail period.

9. List this appeal under the heading "For Hearing" in due course before appropriate Bench.
(Shailendra Singh, J) BKS/-
